## Bonus summary

::: callout-important
## Up to 5 bonus points, for your group

This bonus is optional.
It is worth up to **5 points**, added to one of your four milestone grades.
The points go to **Milestone 4** unless you tell us otherwise when you submit.
They can make up for points you lost on that milestone,
but they cannot take it above its maximum.

It is due with Milestone 4: **2026-12-12 18:00 PT**,
and we grade it from the same `3.0.0` release.
:::

Your project already produces a Quarto report.
For this bonus, you will turn your **whole project into a Quarto website**
and publish it on GitHub Pages.

The website brings together the `README` you have kept up to date all term
and your report.
It replaces the report you published on GitHub Pages in Milestone 2,
at the same URL.

Your website will have:

1.  a **homepage** that is your `README`
2.  your **report**, in both HTML and PDF
3.  an **about** page that introduces each member of your team
4.  a **GitHub icon** in the top right of the menu bar that links to your repository

You will also make one `make` command build everything,
from downloading the data to publishing the website.

This bonus applies what you learned in the DSCI 521 chapter
[Introduction to Quarto and GitHub Pages](https://ubc-mds.github.io/DSCI_521_platforms-dsci_book/lectures/quarto-github-pages.html),
with the same setup:
a `_quarto.yml` in the root of your repository that renders a website into `docs/`.
Read it again first.

## 1. Turn your project into a website

Your project's `_quarto.yml`, in the root of your repository,
already tells Quarto how to render your report.
Turn it into a website's configuration:
add `type: website` and `output-dir: docs`,
list the website's pages in `render`,
and add a `website` section with the menu bar.
Keep the `format` settings you already have
(for example, `embed-resources` and the PDF settings):
they still apply to your report.

Here is a starting point.
Change the title, the report's file name and the repository URL to your own:

```{.yaml filename="_quarto.yml"}
project:
  type: website
  output-dir: docs
  render:
    - index.qmd
    - about.qmd
    - reports/<your-report>.qmd

website:
  title: "Your project title"
  navbar:
    left:
      - href: index.qmd
        text: Home
      - href: reports/<your-report>.qmd
        text: Report
      - href: about.qmd
        text: About
    right:
      - icon: github
        href: https://github.com/UBC-MDS-2026-27/<your-repository>
        aria-label: GitHub repository

# Keep your existing `format:` settings below.
```

The `render` list keeps files like `CONTRIBUTING.md` out of the website.
Give each new page `format: html` in its YAML header,
so that Quarto does not also make a PDF of it
when your project renders your report to PDF.

As in the DSCI 521 chapter,
create an empty `.nojekyll` file in the root of your repository
(see [Turning off Jekyll with `.nojekyll`](https://ubc-mds.github.io/DSCI_521_platforms-dsci_book/lectures/quarto-github-pages.html#nojekyll)).
Quarto copies it into `docs/` every time you render.
Add `.quarto/` to your `.gitignore` if it is not there already.

Your repository will look something like this
(only the new and changed parts are shown):

```
.
├── _quarto.yml           # now a website: renders everything into docs/
├── .nojekyll
├── Makefile
├── README.md
├── index.qmd             # homepage: includes README.md
├── about.qmd             # the team
├── reports/
│   └── <your-report>.qmd
└── docs/                 # the published website (generated, but committed)
    ├── index.html
    └── reports/
        ├── <your-report>.html
        └── <your-report>.pdf
```

::: callout-important
## Your report now renders into `docs/`

Your report is now a page of the website.
Quarto writes it to `docs/reports/<your-report>.html` and `.pdf`,
with the website's menu bar,
instead of next to the `.qmd` in `reports/`.
Delete the old rendered files from `reports/`,
and update your `Makefile` and `README` to the new locations.
This bonus is graded from the same `3.0.0` release as Milestone 4,
so your Milestone 4 `README` instructions must still work exactly as written.
:::

`quarto render` now renders the whole website.
To render just your report while you work on it,
`quarto render reports/<your-report>.qmd` still works,
and `quarto preview` shows the website as you edit it.

## 2. The homepage, the about page and the report

### The homepage (`index.qmd`)

Your `README` already says what your project is, who made it, and how to run it,
so make it your homepage.
`index.qmd` only needs to include it,
using Quarto's [`include` shortcode](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/includes.html):

```{.markdown filename="index.qmd"}
---
format: html
---

{{{< include README.md >}}}
```

You don't need a `title`:
Quarto uses the first heading of your `README` as the page title.
Including the file, rather than copying it,
means the homepage stays up to date whenever your `README` changes.

::: callout-warning
## Links in your `README` must work on the website too

The website only publishes its pages, not the rest of your repository.
A relative link in your `README` to a file such as `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `LICENSE.md` or `src/`
works on GitHub but is broken on the website,
and Quarto does not warn you about it.
Link to those files with their full GitHub URL instead
(for example, `https://github.com/UBC-MDS-2026-27/<your-repository>/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md`),
which works in both places.
:::

### The about page (`about.qmd`)

The about page lists and introduces each member of your team.
For each person, include:

-   their name, linked to their GitHub profile
-   a few sentences introducing them, in their own words
    (for example, their background before MDS and what interests them in data science)

Your website is public,
so each person decides what they share about themselves.
A photo is optional.

### The report

The menu bar's **Report** item links to `reports/<your-report>.qmd`,
and Quarto turns that into a link to the rendered page.
When your report also renders to PDF,
Quarto adds a link to the PDF version on the report's page.
Link to both versions from your `README` too,
so they show up on the homepage.

Every figure in your report and on your website needs **alt text**:
a short description of what the figure shows, for readers who cannot see it.
Use the `fig-alt` option on code cells that make figures,
and the `fig-alt` attribute on images:

```{.markdown}
![Feature densities.](../results/figures/densities.png){#fig-densities fig-alt="Density plots of each feature by class."}
```

See [Alt text](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/figures.html#alt-text) in the Quarto documentation.

## 3. One `make` command builds everything {#make}

Your `Makefile` from Milestone 4 already runs your analysis.
Extend it so that `make all`, run from a fresh clone inside your container,
does everything, in order:

1.  downloads the data
2.  runs your data validation checks
3.  runs the rest of your analysis
4.  publishes: renders the website, including your report, into `docs/`

`make clean` should remove everything that `make all` creates, including `docs/`.

In Milestone 4, your `publish` target copied your report to `docs/index.html`,
and `make all` ran it.
For the bonus, change the rule behind `publish` so that it renders the website instead,
and remove your old rule for the report in `reports/`:
the report now renders as part of the website.
Here is a sketch.
Change the file names to your own,
and list as prerequisites every file the website reads,
including your `README` and the figures and tables your report shows,
so `make` rebuilds the website when one of them changes:

```{.makefile filename="Makefile"}
.DELETE_ON_ERROR:

publish: docs/index.html

docs/index.html: _quarto.yml index.qmd README.md about.qmd \
		reports/<your-report>.qmd results/figures/<your-figure>.png
	quarto render

clean:
	rm -rf docs
	# ... and everything else your pipeline creates
```

`quarto render` empties `docs/` before it renders,
so no pages are left over from an older version of the website.
`.DELETE_ON_ERROR:` makes `make` delete `docs/index.html` if the render fails partway.
Without it, the next `make` would find a `docs/index.html`
and say there is nothing to do.

::: callout-important
## A clean build, with no warnings

Before you submit, run `make clean` and then `make all` inside your container.
Everything should rebuild, and Quarto should print **no `ERROR` or `WARN` messages**
(for example, about links it could not find).
Messages from other tools, such as Jupyter, don't count.
We will grade this bonus by doing the same.
:::

Update your `README` to say how to build the website.

## 4. Publish on GitHub Pages

The `docs/` folder is generated, but commit it anyway:
GitHub Pages can only publish files that are in your repository.
This is the one generated folder you commit.
Check that `docs/.nojekyll` is there, on your computer (`ls -a docs`) and on GitHub.com.

Since Milestone 2, GitHub Pages has published your report from the `main` branch and the `/docs` folder.
Keep that setting.
Your website now replaces the report at the same URL:
the homepage is at `https://ubc-mds-2026-27.github.io/<your-repository>/`,
and the report moves to `https://ubc-mds-2026-27.github.io/<your-repository>/reports/<your-report>.html`.
Update the report link in your `README`,
and say in your `README`, and in the **About** box on your repository's GitHub page,
that the URL is now your project's website.

## Submission instructions

Submit on Gradescope, under the bonus assignment.
We only need URLs and one answer, entered into Gradescope directly: there is no PDF to make.
You will submit:

1.  the URL of your published website
2.  the URL of your project's GitHub.com repository
3.  the URL of your `3.0.0` release
4.  which milestone the bonus points should go to (Milestone 4 if you leave it blank)

## Rubric

Each item is worth 1 point.

| Points | Item                                                                         |
|--------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1 | The website is published on GitHub Pages from `docs/`. The menu bar has Home, Report and About, and a GitHub icon at the top right that links to the repository. |
| 1 | The homepage includes the `README` (not a copy of it), and every link in it works on the website. |
| 1 | The report is a page of the website, in HTML and PDF, and the `Makefile` and `README` use its new location. Every figure in the report has alt text. |
| 1 | The about page introduces each team member. |
| 1 | From a fresh clone, inside the container, `make all` runs the whole analysis and builds the website with the report, and Quarto prints no `ERROR` or `WARN` messages. `make clean` removes everything `make all` creates, including `docs/`. |
